In-context: The RTF document exploits CVE-2017-11882 to execute shellcode that connects to a malicious host and downloads the payload. The payload is saved in a folder created by the shellcode and runs as a process on the victim's machine.

The malicious RTF document contains an embedded OLE object with the class name 'Equation 3.0'. When opened with Microsoft Word, it invokes the Equation Editor to execute the equation formula containing shellcode. This shellcode exploits a vulnerability to download and execute the payload on the victim's machine.

The malware's information-gathering function collects the victim's hostname, operating system product name, and username. It then writes this information into a memory buffer to be sent to the command and control server.
The payload runs as a Windows security update service on the victim's machine and establishes communication with the C2 to remotely download and execute files in the victim's environment.

In the case of a malicious Excel spreadsheet, when the victim opens the file, it launches the Microsoft Equation Editor application to execute the embedded equation object and launches the task scheduler to configure two scheduled tasks.
